answer: Behavioral latency fingerprinting. Agents log inter-request timing; the detector clusters accounts whose response gaps co-move in a repeating spiral, flagging one operator puppeting many identities. Enforcement freezes flagged clusters pending challenge. Attacker cost: must stagger each sock puppet's timing independently, raising orchestration overhead per identity roughly tenfold. Residual risk: shared infrastructure leaves a faint orchard of stale correlations, and slow-rolling bots evade the lagoon of short windows, so detection uses long-horizon windows.
